system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

[CAPCP#0087] Canadian Profile of the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP-CP): Introduction and Rule Set 1.0 (Draft 2) (Rule #6. A recognized <eventCode> must be used):
There is a limit of one <eventCode> value from the CAP-CP Event References list per alert message even though multiple occurrences of the element <eventCode> may appear in an alert message.

[CAPCP#0035] Canadian Profile of the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP-CP): Introduction and Rule Set 1.0 (Draft 2) (Constraint of one subject event per alert message):
Constraint of one subject event per alert message The Reference Standard allows for the inclusion of multiple subject events within a single CAP alert message, but specifies only one unique CAP message identifier is required. Therefore, a situational change to any one of the subject events, triggering a new CAP message update, would give the appearance of a change to any and all of the other subject events within the update message. Further, given that event values will be used for the purpose of filtering, routing, validating, and other needs within the community; systems could have difficulty handling a single alert message containing multiple subject events when the information associated to a subset of the subject events may be changing. To avoid any potential confusion, the CAP-CP limits each CAP alert message to one subject event value.

[TS23041#0421] 3GPP TS 23.041 Technical realization of Cell Broadcast Service (CBS), version 18.3.0 Release 18 (ETSI TS 123 041 V18.3.0) (p.84):
9.4.1.2.4 Page Parameter This parameter is coded as two 4-bit fields. The first field (bits 0-3) indicates the binary value of the total number of pages in the CBS message and the second field (bits 4-7) indicates binary the page number within that sequence. The coding starts at 0001, with 0000 reserved. If a mobile receives the code 0000 in either the first field or the second field then it shall treat the CBS message exactly the same as a CBS message with page parameter 0001 0001 (i.e. a single page message).

Any remaining octets after the compression footer shall contain padding up to and including the 82nd octet position. However, if the 82nd octet position contains the compression footer then there is no padding. In the case where compression applies across multiple 'CBS-Message-Information-Page's, the compression header shall be present only in the first octet position of the first 'CBS-Message-Information-Page'. The compression footer shall immediately follow the compressed data stream which will terminate within the last 'CBS-Message-Infirmation-Page'. Any remaining octets after the compression footer in the last 'CBS-Message-Information-Page' shall contain padding up to and including the 82nd octet position in the last 'CBS-Message-Information-Page'. However, if the 82nd octet position of the last 'CBS-Message-Information-Page' contains the compression footer then there is no padding. If it is required to convey different blocks of information which are to be treated by the MS/UE as though they were physically independent pages rather than concatenated information then page break characters (see 3GPP TS 23.038 [3]) may be inserted in the character stream prior to compression.

data.summary: Neither language can be delivered under the UAE profile: English needs 4 pages and Arabic needs 7, against a 1-page limit. The text also combines two different events. The dust/sand advisory comes first and gives no action. An unverified dam-burst evacuation order ('Reports say…; leave the area now') comes last, on the final page, so it would be lost on any one-page cut. A person needs to decide whether the dam burst is confirmed and whether it should be a separate, higher-priority alert. The drafter cannot settle that alone.

objections.issue: Both language versions exceed the UAE one-page handset limit. English is GSM-7, 282 characters, 4 pages. Arabic is UCS-2, 287 characters, 7 pages. A single 82-octet page holds about 93 GSM-7 characters or about 41 UCS-2 characters.
objections.fix: Rewrite each language to fit one page: about 93 characters or fewer in English (GSM-7) and about 41 characters or fewer in Arabic (UCS-2). Keep only the hazard, the area, the action and the expiry time. Move background and source to a longer channel or a linked page.

evidence.quote: Message should be limited to 1 page maximum.
message should be limited to 1 page
the BSC sends to the BTS in one single message the 88 octet fixed length CBS page

objections.issue: The first page does not carry an action. The dust/sand hazard has no instruction at all. The only action in the message ('leave the area now') sits in the last sentence of both languages, so it falls on the final page and would be cut by any one-page reduction.
objections.fix: Lead each language with the hazard and the protective action in the first words, for example 'Dust storm, visibility under 2 km: avoid driving' in English, with the Arabic equivalent. Do not leave any action after the first page.

evidence.quote: Reports say a dam near Al Ain has burst; leave the area now.
تفيد التقارير بانهيار سد قرب العين؛ غادروا المنطقة فوراً.

objections.issue: One broadcast mixes two separate events: an NCM-sourced dust/sand advisory and an unsourced 'reports say' dam burst with an evacuation order. The dam-burst order is the most urgent item, yet it has no stated source and is buried at the end. Whether it is confirmed, and whether it needs its own higher-priority alert and area, is a decision for the issuing authority, not the drafter.
objections.fix: Escalate to the issuing authority. If the dam burst is confirmed, send it as its own one-page alert with the evacuation action first and a targeted area. Remove it from the dust advisory either way.

no_basis.concern: The stated English page count (4) is higher than the roughly 3 pages that 282 GSM-7 characters would need at about 93 characters per page. This may come from the counting tool or from extended characters, and is worth checking.
